item.title: Study Hall: Spirits & Signatures — Wed Nov 4, 6:30 PM — The Conway Room
item.description: You know the names. You know the drinks. But do you know the stories behind them? Join us at The Conway Room for Spirits & Signatures, a playful, interactive evening exploring the trademarks, iconic cocktails, and recognizable brands that have shaped drinking culture through the years. From signature drinks to the stories behind some of the world’s best-known spirits brands, this Study Hall takes a closer look at how cocktails and trademarks become icons. Discover the history, branding, and culture behind familiar names while putting your own knowledge to the test along the way. Expect an engaging mix of cocktail education, surprising stories, and interactive fun—all in the welcoming atmosphere of The Conway Room. Whether you’re a cocktail enthusiast, a curious sipper, or simply interested in the stories behind the brands you know, there’s something new to discover. item.title: LFS Feminist Consciousness-Raising Film Afternoons — Sun Nov 15, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Lancaster Freethought Society **Feminist Film Afternoons #1: Made in Dagenham (2010)**
**What happens when women stop cooperating with a system that depends on their labor but refuses to value it?** Join us for the first of five Feminist Consciousness-Raising Film Afternoons, featuring *Made in Dagenham*, the spirited, funny, and inspiring true story of women workers at Ford's Dagenham factory in England. In 1968, women sewing machinists discover that their work has been classified as unskilled and paid less than men's. Rather than accept it, they organize, strike, and help launch a movement for equal pay. **After the film, we'll discuss:**
* What changed when these women recognized their shared situation? * Why was withdrawing their labor more effective than simply demanding fair treatment? * What could women accomplish today by collectively withdrawing their cooperation from unequal systems?
This is a relaxed, friendly afternoon of film and conversation—not a lecture or debate. Ev

item.title: Lincoln and the Founders: Completing the Unfinished Work — Thu Nov 19, 6:30 PM — Columbia
item.description:
Community, Presentation, Teens, Adults, Seniors, Everyone
In the Gettysburg Address, Abraham Lincoln said that the nation should be dedicated "to the unfinished work which they who fought here have thus far so nobly advanced." What was this unfinished work? When Lincoln started his famous address with "Four score and seven years ago," he hearkened back to the year 1776 and the Declaration of Independence that stated that "all men are created equal."Much of Lincoln's political ideology stemmed from the Declaration of Independence. His words and policies before and during the Civil War demonstrate his reverence for the Declaration. While Lincoln was not an abolitionist, he did believe that slavery should be put in "the course of ultimate extinction" by preventing its spread to the territories.As President, Lincoln originally worked to preserve the Union that the Founders created. item.title: LFS Feminist Consciousness-Raising Film Afternoons — Sun Nov 29, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Lancaster Freethought Society **Feminist Film Afternoons #2: Salt of the Earth (1954)**
**What happens when women discover that fighting for their families isn't enough—they must fight for their own equality, too?** Join us for the second of five Feminist Consciousness-Raising Film Afternoons, featuring *Salt of the Earth*, a groundbreaking American film based on a real miners' strike in New Mexico. When Mexican-American miners strike against dangerous working conditions and discriminatory wages, a court injunction prevents the men from picketing. Their wives step forward to take their places, while the men must assume responsibility for the households and children. What begins as support for their husbands becomes something much more powerful: women discovering their own political agency. **After the film, we'll discuss:**

Together we can help each other grow and expand our consciousness for these high vibrational times.

item.title: Evening Compline — Fri Oct 30, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Carlson Kids! Art at the Library! — Sat Jan 23, 10:30 AM — Quarryville
item.description:
Arts & Crafts, Children, Tweens
Ages 6-12, children under 8 should have responsible caregiver present.Our main program room is named for Charles X. Carlson, the notable local artist. And what more fitting purpose than to use it to inspire a new generation of artists! Carlson Kids is a new grant-funded program that brings together a local art teacher, some aspiring teen coaches, and young future artists! Students will do art activities in similar styles to Charlie Carlson's work, which includes watercolor, collage, cartooning, and some experimental projects. This program will be offered on one Thursday afternoon and one Saturday afternoon per month. You may register for any sessions you wish, attendance at all sessions is not mandatory. We gratefully acknowledge the C. X. Carlson Cultural Trust Fund for their generosity in providing this program to our community.
Source: Lancaster Libraries

item.title: Duplo Free Play — Sat Jan 23, 11:00 AM — Manheim Township
item.description:
STEM, Toddlers, Children
Drop-in program. No registration required.Join us for a fun and engaging play session designed for children ages 2-7! Using colorful Lego Duplo blocks, kids can explore their creativity, improve fine motor skills, and build their imagination through hands-on play. This program encourages collaborative play and parent-child interaction.Perfect for young builders of all skill levels, this free program offers a relaxed and welcoming environment for families to connect and create together. Come play, learn, and grow at the library! Each family group must include a responsible adult in the room at all times. This program is for children 2 to 7 years old only! While other ages are welcome in the room, we kindly ask that the play area and toys remain reserved exclusively for the intended age group to ensure a safe environment for young participants.
